tool_defs.name: edit
tool_defs.description: Write a file, or change part of one. Two ways to call it, and you pick one or the other: pass `content` to write a whole file, creating it if it doesn't exist and replacing it entirely if it does (parent folders are made for you) — that's how you create a new file or rewrite one you've outgrown. Pass `edits` to change text inside a file that already exists, leaving the rest alone; prefer this when you're correcting or adding to something, so you don't lose what's already there. Each edit's old_string must match exactly, whitespace and newlines included, so read the file first if you're unsure what's in it. By default old_string must match exactly once — add surrounding context to make it unique, or set replace_all to replace every occurrence. `edits` on a file that doesn't exist is an error rather than a new file: if you meant to create it, say so with `content`.

content.description: Full content for the file, creating it or overwriting it wholesale. Parent directories are created automatically. Mutually exclusive with `edits`.

edits.description: List of replacements to apply in order to an existing file. Mutually exclusive with `content`.

old_string.description: Exact text to find and replace. Must match whitespace and newlines precisely.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of old_string. Defaults to false, which requires old_string to match exactly once.

prepare_chat_context.note: the three sources in one surface, with templating applied to the subagent

s0.description: Read a file, or see what's in a directory. Point it at a file and it returns the content as text; point it at a directory and it lists what's there, with each entry's name, type, and size. Omit the path entirely to list your workspace root. Use offset and limit to page through a large file. Reach for this when you're looking for something by name, date, or where it sits in your folders — `search` is for fuzzy content matching, this is for exact lookups and for reading what you found.
s0.name: read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read. Files only; ignored for directories. Optional.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-based). Files only; ignored for directories. Optional.

path.description: Relative path within your workspace. A file path returns its contents; a directory path lists its entries. Omit for a listing of the workspace root.
